title: Vulnerability Analysis

objectives.text: Classify a weakness (misconfiguration, default credentials, missing patch, buffer overflow, design flaw, zero-day) and link it to its CWE or OWASP category
Tell CVE, NVD, CWE, CAPEC, CPE, CVSS, EPSS and KEV apart: who runs each one and what question it answers
Read a CVSS v3.1 vector string, give its severity band, and name what CVSS v4.0 changed (AT, UI values, no Scope, Threat group, supplemental metrics)
Put the vulnerability-management life cycle in order, from asset inventory and baseline to verification and monitoring
Choose the right assessment type and scanning approach (credentialed, agent-based, passive, internal or external) for a scenario
Recognize Nessus, OpenVAS/Greenbone, Nikto, Nmap NSE, OWASP ZAP, Nuclei, Trivy and Lynis from their output, options or ports
Explain what AI adds to vulnerability assessment and the rules for using it with client data
Validate findings (false positives and false negatives), prioritize them with KEV, EPSS and asset context, and pick a risk response
Structure a vulnerability assessment report for managers and for the teams who fix the findings

readingMap.why: CVSS metrics and bands, CVE vs CWE vs NVD, KEV and EPSS, and the life cycle order are the bulk of this module's questions.
Tool-identification and scanning-approach scenarios (credentialed, agent, passive) come up often; learn the tool table, skip vendor feature lists.
Know the report parts, false positive vs false negative, and how to rank findings; the sample report layouts add little.

labs.name: Research one CVE end to end: NVD record, CVSS vector, CWE, EPSS score and KEV status
labs.skill: Reading a CVSS vector and combining severity, exploitation probability and known exploitation into a priority

labs.name: Install Greenbone Community Edition on Kali and scan a Metasploitable 2 VM in your own isolated lab
labs.skill: Setting up gvm, running a scan, reading results with QoD, separating true and false positives

labs.name: Compare an unauthenticated and a credentialed Nessus Essentials scan of your own lab VM
labs.skill: Seeing how credentials change findings, false positives and patch-level accuracy

labs.name: Scan DVWA in your own lab with Nikto, then with OWASP ZAP, and compare the findings
labs.skill: Telling web server findings (Nikto) apart from web application findings (ZAP) and reading Nikto tuning and output options

feynmanPrompts: Explain to a manager why a CVSS 9.8 finding on a lab server can wait while a CVSS 7.5 finding on the VPN gateway must be fixed this week.
Explain the difference between CVE, CWE and CVSS using one real vulnerability as the example.
Walk through the vulnerability-management life cycle for one missing patch, from asset inventory to the monitoring that proves it stays fixed.
